Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

tikatuwq 0.11.0

Scientific stabilization of the IQA core and of the trophic state indices. IQA and IET values change for some inputs; see inst/audit/IQA_AUDITORIA.md and inst/audit/REGRESSAO_0_10_0_0_11_0.csv for the full before/after comparison.

This release also includes: - a breaking change: the classification argument of iqa() was removed (see “Calculation engines and comparison”); - a new IGAM engine, iqa(method = "IGAM"), which is a documented reproduction and is not endorsed by IGAM; - compare_iqa().

CETESB (2023) Appendix D gives the IQA sub-indices only as graphical curves (Figure 1). The package’s piecewise equations come from the CETESB spreadsheet as transcribed by CPRH (PNMA II) and by von Sperling (2007, p. 255; reproduced by IBEAS 2015). Weights, fixed out-of-range values, unit conversions and the classification match the official text exactly; where the two secondary transcriptions disagree, the choice follows the official curve. An independent re-implementation agrees with iqa() to 1e-14 on 3000 inputs, and the published IBEAS/von Sperling worked example (IQA = 81) is reproduced.

Changes in numerical results

  • .qi_cetesb_ph(), 8.5 < pH <= 9: 10^(-1.1507 pH) replaced by exp(-1.1507 pH). The old form gave qi ~ 0.0002 at pH 8.6. Example: wq_demo point FBS-BRH-300 on 2023-05-24 moves from 15.58 (Pessima) to 82.55 (Otima).
  • .qi_cetesb_ph(), 9 < pH <= 10: 50 - 32 (pH - 9) replaced by 288 - 27 pH (removes the 45 -> 50 jump at pH 9; Figure 1 has no jump there). CPRH prints 228 - 27 pH (an evident typo: it would give qi < 0), while von Sperling via IBEAS gives the old form. Effect on the IQA: at most 0.9 point. Maintainer decision pending.
  • .qi_cetesb_dbo(), 5 < DBO <= 15 mg/L, and .qi_cetesb_nt(), 10 < NT <= 60 mg/L: log10() replaced by natural log(), removing the jumps at 5/15 and 10/60 mg/L. IQA drops by up to ~9 points (DBO) and ~15 points (NT) in these ranges. Figure 1 confirms the corrected values (e.g. BOD 10 mg/L: ~30, was 73). Note: spreadsheets that follow the von Sperling (2007) transcription with log10 (e.g. IBEAS 2015) give higher IQA values in these ranges.
  • DO saturation Cs: cubic coefficient 0.00005898 corrected to 0.00005896 (CPRH; von Sperling via IBEAS). Effect below 0.02% of Cs.
  • .qi_cetesb_temperatura(): delta T < -5 C now gives NA (qi is “undefined” per Figure 1); it returned 93. temperature_method = "delta"/"reference" now warns that the package’s delta-T curve does not match the CETESB curve; these modes are experimental and flagged in attr(, "iqa_nonstandard"). The default (qi = 94: CPRH and IBEAS “constant of 94 adopted by CETESB”; consistent with the source’s q^w = 1.58) is unchanged.
  • iqa() now assigns IQA_status from the unrounded IQA; rounding to two decimals is display only (e.g. 79.004 is Otima although shown as 79.00).
  • iet_lamparelli(): now uses the Lamparelli (2004) equations given by CETESB (Appendix D 2023, p. 10), different for rivers and reservoirs, with total phosphorus and chlorophyll-a in ug/L. Until v0.10.0 it used 10 + 10 log10(x) for both environments, which classified almost any sample as ultraoligotrophic (e.g. TP = 137 ug/L in a river gave 1.4 instead of 59.5). Results now reproduce the class limits of Tables 5 and 6. Secchi depth is returned as an auxiliary component and no longer enters IET_Lamp, as CETESB does not use transparency.
  • iet_carlson(): natural logarithm instead of log10 (Carlson 1977 defines TSI = 10 (6 - log2 SD); the 14.41/14.42/9.81 coefficients only hold with ln). Example: TP = 48 ug/L now gives 60 (was 28.4).
  • generate_analysis(): the dominant IQA class now uses the CETESB scale of classify_iqa() instead of a private 25/50/70/90 scale, and the text reports how many samples are partial IQA estimates.
  • plot_map_quality(): auto-detection now recognizes IET_Lamp, the column returned by iet_lamparelli() (it only looked for IET_Lamparelli, so Lamparelli output was never detected; the corresponding test was silently skipped).
  • Physically invalid inputs (negative concentrations, pH outside 0-14, temperature outside -2..50 C, Inf) now become NA with a warning instead of being silently truncated to 0 (which gave the best possible qi).

Calculation engines and comparison

  • New iqa_methods() lists the IQA calculation engines and their validation status.
  • New iqa(df, method = "IGAM"): an engine independent of the CETESB one, giving a documented computational reproduction of the IGAM (Minas Gerais) IQA. It is not endorsed by IGAM.
    • Sources: SCQA equations (SEMAD/UCEMG/PNMA II 2005, Relatorio 1; the copy IGAM hosted, SHA-1 verified) and the Projeto Aguas de Minas rules: temperature qs = 92; no index without dissolved oxygen or the microbial parameter; other missing weights shared equally.
    • Turbidity: uses the coefficient 1.5 in the cosine term, as recorded by Bucci (2011, p. 51) and Nunes (2008, Table 10). Copies of the SCQA print
    • Validation: reproduces all 49 IQA values published by IGAM for the Pampulha sub-basin, after rounding to one decimal place (maximum unrounded error 0.049). Fifteen of them come from the 3rd quarter of 2017 and were used in the investigation. The other 34 come from the 3rd quarter of 2018 and the 4th quarter of 2017, selected with pre-registered criteria.
    • Strict inputs (no unit is assumed):
      • nitrate_unit (“N” or “NO3”) is required with nitrate;
      • p_total requires phosphorus_basis, while fosfato_total (PO4) is used as is;
      • chloride is required for oxygen saturation, with no default;
      • if both E. coli and thermotolerant coliforms are present, microbial_type must choose one;
      • allow_partial, pesos and the CETESB temperature options raise an error.
    • Output: the IQA is rounded to one decimal place, as IGAM publishes it. Censoring is recorded per row.
    • Data not redistributed: the 49 historical records are IGAM data and do not ship with the package. The methodology note documents the aggregate metrics, the sources (with SHA-1) and how to reproduce the check. The package tests use synthetic data, with expected values computed independently.
    • See system.file("methodology", "IGAM_VALIDATION.md", package = "tikatuwq").
  • iqa_methods(): IGAM is available = TRUE and reference_validated = TRUE. reference_validated is now documented as reproducing values published by the reference institution, within the scope stated in limitation. It is not endorsement or validation in every basin.
  • compare_iqa() now compares CETESB and IGAM on paired samples.
  • iqa_components(method = "IGAM") points to iqa(df, method = "IGAM", details = TRUE).
  • New argument nitrate_unit in iqa(), used only by IGAM.
  • New column alias cloreto (chloride, mg/L).
  • New compare_iqa(): runs each engine on the same rows, keeps row identity (id_cols), reports eligibility and reasons per method, and computes paired statistics (mean/median difference, MAE, RMSE, correlations with >= 3 pairs) only on rows valid for all methods. Class differences are reported as a transition table, not as label agreement. Unavailable methods make all rows ineligible instead of failing.
  • Breaking: iqa() no longer has a classification argument (it existed in 0.10.0 with "cetesb"/"legacy"). The scale follows method; passing classification or scheme is an error that points to classify_iqa(iqa(df)$IQA, classification = ...). Positional calls from 0.10.0 with the classification as third argument (iqa(df, "CETESB", "legacy")) now fail with the same migration message, because the third argument is now altitude_m. classify_iqa() is unchanged. New attributes iqa_calculation_method and iqa_method_version.
  • iqa_methods() reports implemented, documented, reference_validated, available and limitation for each engine.
  • New canonical column fosfato_total (total phosphate as PO4), distinct from p_ortofosfato and p_total.
  • ANA: no method = "ANA" (see inst/audit/ANA_VS_CETESB.md); classify_iqa(classification = "ana") stays.

nsfwqi()

  • Documented as an approximation by coarse step functions, not the validated NSF WQI (sub-index maximum is 90, so the index never exceeds 90; DO in mg/L). New attribute nsfwqi_validation.
  • With na_rm = FALSE, a component without a column now gives NA, as documented (it was silently dropped with renormalized weights). All 20 wq_demo rows (no nitrate, no total solids) change from a value to NA in strict mode; partial (na_rm = TRUE) values are unchanged (inst/audit/REGRESSAO_NSFWQI_0_11_0.csv).
  • Total suspended solids are no longer used as total solids (warning).

API

  • classify_iqa() now uses classification (same name as in iqa()). scheme still works but is deprecated (warning); giving both with different values is an error. iqa() also accepts scheme via ... with the same rules.
  • New classification scales "igam" (25/50/70/90) and "ana". "ana" uses the 19/36/51/79 cuts shown on the current ANA portal and is an alias of "cetesb". classification never changes the numeric IQA.
  • classify_iqa() returns NA (with a warning) for values outside [0, 100]; previously they were classified as the lowest/highest class.
  • iqa() now forwards delta_temperature (it was silently ignored). temperature_method = "delta" without a delta, or "reference" without temperature_reference, is now an error instead of silently using qi = 94.
  • pesos: must be a named, finite, non-negative vector of known parameter names. Unknown names (e.g. tds) were silently ignored before and are now an error. With details = TRUE, the wi_* and term_* columns hold the effective (renormalized) weights, so prod(qi^wi) reproduces the IQA.
  • allow_partial = TRUE: partial rows are listed in attr(, "iqa_partial_rows") and, with details = TRUE, in the new IQA_partial/missing_params columns. This is a package estimate, not an institutional rule.
  • altitude_m accepts one value per row; values outside -500..9000 m are an error.
  • na_rm in iqa() is deprecated in favour of allow_partial. Unknown arguments passed through ... now produce a warning.
  • New provenance attributes on iqa() output, including for empty input and the legacy routes: iqa_method_reference, iqa_weights, iqa_custom_weights, iqa_allow_partial, iqa_partial_rows, iqa_nonstandard. iqa_complete now reports whether every computed row was complete (it used to echo !allow_partial).

Documentation

  • Removed unverified claims that the equations are “official”, “validated” and “continuous”. Pending items are listed in inst/audit/IQA_AUDITORIA.md.
  • New sections in ?iqa: method vs classification, missing data, invalid values.
  • ?wq_demo now states that the dataset has TDS but not total solids, so its IQA values are partial estimates (8 parameters), not CETESB IQA values, and that it is not an independent benchmark.

Tests and checks

  • 37 test files, 181 tests and 806 expectations. Includes a CETESB regression baseline (131 cases, inst/audit/REGRESSAO_CETESB_POS_API.csv) and IGAM tests on synthetic samples, whose expected values come from an independent implementation.
  • R CMD check --as-cran: 0 errors and 0 warnings on Windows (local, and win-builder R-devel and R-release), Linux (Ubuntu) and macOS (R-release, Apple silicon). win-builder reports 1 note: the place name “Minas Gerais” in DESCRIPTION is flagged as a possible misspelling.

Known open items

  • CETESB pH 9-10: two published transcriptions differ. The package uses 288 - 27 pH, which is continuous and follows the curve; the alternative is 50 - 32 (pH - 9). The effect is at most 0.9 IQA points, with no class change in the tests. Decision pending.
  • CETESB delta-T curve (temperature_method = "delta"/"reference"): it has no traceable source and stays experimental, with a warning. The default (qi = 94) is not affected.
  • IGAM: no institutional confirmation of the turbidity coefficient 1.5; not validated outside the Pampulha sub-basin; IGAM rules for censored values, missing chloride and rounding are not documented (package policies apply).

tikatuwq 0.10.0

CRAN release: 2026-08-31

Breaking changes and scientific corrections

  • Official CETESB analytical equations: iqa() now implements the official validated continuous piecewise polynomial/exponential equations from CETESB/INEMA rather than discrete/interpolated approximation tables.
  • Total Solids vs TDS: The canonical 9th component of CETESB IQA is now strictly solidos_totais (Total Solids / Resíduo Total, weight 0.08). TDS (tds) is no longer accepted silently as a synonym for Total Solids; providing tds in strict CETESB mode throws an explicit, informative error.
  • Stoichiometric phosphorus conversion: Total phosphorus (mg P/L) is now converted to phosphate via PO4=Ptotal×3.066PO_4 = P_{\text{total}} \times 3.066 by default (phosphorus_basis = "P"), matching the calibration basis of the CETESB sub-index curve.
  • Separation of water temperature and ΔT\Delta T: Water temperature (temperatura) is used exclusively to compute DO saturation percentage (accounting for altitude via altitude_m), while temperature change ΔT\Delta T (delta_temperatura) is an independent component defaulting to Qi=94Q_i = 94 (operational hypothesis of thermal equilibrium).
  • Coliforms & E. coli: Canonical parameter is coliformes_termotolerantes. E. coli inputs are converted using the CETESB factor 1.25×1.25\times via microbial_type = "e_coli".
  • Strict calculation by default: iqa() with method = "CETESB" requires all 9 components. Partial calculation now requires explicit allow_partial = TRUE and flags missing components in metadata.
  • Official CETESB classification scale: Default breaks for classify_iqa() updated to official CETESB categories: Péssima (≤19\le 19), Ruim (19–3619\text{--}36), Regular (36–5136\text{--}51), Boa (51–7951\text{--}79), Ótima (79–10079\text{--}100).

New features

  • iqa_components() and iqa(..., details = TRUE): Comprehensive audit layer returning raw values, transformed values, QiQ_i, WiW_i, and QiWiQ_i^{W_i} for each parameter.
  • Explicit censored data policy (censor_policy = c("limit", "half_limit", "preserve", "zero", "na")).
  • Extensive scientific test suite and benchmark against official INEMA SEIA Campanha 3/2024 (Rio Buranhém) monitoring records.

tikatuwq 0.9.0

CRAN release: 2026-06-09

Breaking changes

  • iqa() now defaults to the correct weighted geometric mean (method = "CETESB") as specified by CETESB and the original NSF WQI (Brown et al., 1970). The previous arithmetic mean behaviour is preserved via method = "NSF_approx". Existing code using iqa() without specifying method will produce different (more accurate) IQA values. (#P0)

New functions

  • mk_seasonal(): seasonal Mann-Kendall trend test (Hirsch, Slack & Smith, 1982). Splits the time series by season (monthly or wet/dry via assign_season()), computes S and VAR(S) per season, aggregates, and returns Z, p-value, Kendall tau, and Sen’s slope (units/year) per group. Removes the seasonal bias that inflates false positives in standard Mann-Kendall tests applied to tropical rivers. (#P6)
  • plot_map_quality(): interactive Leaflet map coloring sampling sites by IQA, IET (Carlson or Lamparelli), or NSF WQI value. Uses the standard classification palettes for each index and shows class and value in the popup. Extends plot_map() with index-aware choropleth logic. (#P12)
  • balnear_check(): classifies sampling sites for primary-contact recreation (swimming) under CONAMA Resolution 274/2000 (Excelente, Muito Boa, Satisfatória, Imprópria) based on the 80% rule over the last 5 collections. Supports thermotolerant coliforms and E. coli; flags sites with insufficient samples. (#P16)
  • conama_freq_check(): implements the legal frequency rule of CONAMA 357/2005 Art. 15 — conformity assessed as ≥80% of samples within limits, requiring at least 6 samples per year. Returns a tibble with per-point, per-year, per-parameter compliance status. (#P1)
  • assign_season(): adds a hydrological season column ("chuvoso" / "seco") to a data frame, based on regional Brazilian calendars (Sudeste, Nordeste, Norte, Sul, Centro-Oeste, Bahia) or a custom month vector. (#P3)
  • compare_seasons(): compares a water quality parameter between wet and dry seasons using Wilcoxon, t-test, or Kruskal-Wallis; returns descriptive statistics, test results, and optionally a ggplot boxplot. (#P3)
  • plot_iet(): bar chart (vertical or horizontal) for the Trophic State Index with color-coded trophic classes, supporting both Carlson (1977) and Lamparelli (2004) classification schemes. (#P4)
  • compute_load(): computes pollutant load as concentration × flow × unit factor; supports kg/day, t/day, kg/year, and g/s outputs. (#P7)
  • exceedance_prob(): estimates empirical exceedance probability with Wilson confidence interval, by group. (#P8)
  • wq_pca(): PCA wrapper around stats::prcomp() with automatic column selection, biplot, screeplot, and loadings plot as ggplot attributes. (#P15)
  • nsfwqi(): updated to use weighted geometric mean (consistent with CETESB IQA fix), adds add_status and locale arguments, removes prototype language. (#P5)

Data

  • inst/extdata/conama_limits.csv expanded from ~38 to ~116 rows, adding nitrogen species (NO3, NO2, NH3 with pH-conditional limits), inorganic ions (fluorides, chlorides, sulfates), organic pollutants (phenols, surfactants), and 14 heavy metals / trace elements for Classes 1–3. (#P2)

Internal

  • R/testando.R: replaced empty file with documented placeholder comment.
  • R/wq_buranhem.R: removed duplicate @docType tag that caused a R CMD check WARNING.
  • DESCRIPTION: version bumped to 0.9.0; tools added to Imports.
  • Tests added for all new modules (test-iqa-geometric.R, test-conama_freq.R, test-seasonal.R, test-load_exceedance.R, test-plot_iet.R, test-wq_pca.R).

tikatuwq 0.8.2

CRAN release: 2026-01-16

  • CRAN maintenance: Patch release for CRAN compliance. Fixed example in plot_map() to use internal dataset wq_demo instead of external file reference. All examples and tests now comply with CRAN policies (no local file dependencies, write only to tempdir). No API changes.

tikatuwq 0.8.1

  • Fix (CRAN compliance): render_report() now copies the template to a temporary directory before rendering to comply with CRAN filesystem policies. All intermediate files generated during rendering are written only to output_dir (default tempdir()), never to the package installation directory. Tests for render_report() are now skipped on CRAN (skip_on_cran()) and use withr::local_tempdir() for proper cleanup.

tikatuwq 0.8.0

CRAN release: 2025-11-17

  • Data and documentation update: The wq_demo example dataset is now a subset of real data (from BURANHEM river monitoring, 4 points, years 2020–2024, 20 rows). Includes extra columns: rio, lat, and lon.
  • All examples and vignettes now use real, representative dataset (greater realism and reproducibility).
  • Documentation (R/data_wq_demo.R, inst/extdata/wq_demo_README.txt, vignettes, README) updated to reflect the change.
  • No API breakage; all functions and test expectations remain valid for the new dataset structure and size.

tikatuwq 0.7.3

CRAN release: 2025-10-31

  • Funções iet_carlson() e iet_lamparelli() agora aceitam data.frame com .keep_ids.
  • Conversão automática de formato BR (“,” / “<” / “>”) e de p_total (mg/L) → tp (µg/L).
  • iqa() mais robusto: alias temp para temperatura, numificação segura e reponderação com na_rm=TRUE.
  • Campos identificadores (rio, ponto, data, lat, lon) agora são automaticamente reconhecidos e preservados via .keep_ids.

tikatuwq 0.7.2

CRAN release: 2025-10-22

Changes in this version: - Fixed incoming NOTE detected in pre-tests: - Removed non-standard fields (DOI, Citation) from DESCRIPTION. - Updated inst/CITATION to use the modern bibentry() format instead of the deprecated citEntry(). - Minor internal documentation updates (no API or functional changes).

tikatuwq 0.7.1

  • Title field adjusted per CRAN request: now “Water Quality Assessment and Environmental Compliance in Brazil”.

tikatuwq 0.7.0

  • New functions param_analysis() and param_analysis_multi():
    • Enable detailed analysis of specific parameters by point, river, or group of points.
    • Support cross-comparisons (multiple parameters at one point or multiple points for the same parameter).
    • Include simple temporal trend detection and basic statistical summary.
    • Return standardized data frames compatible with visualization and reporting tools.
  • Automated tests for new modules (test-param_analysis.R, test-param_analysis_multi.R).
  • Code updated to meet CRAN best practices (all checks passed 100% cleanly).
  • Minor stability improvements in plot_trend() and plot_map() (controlled messages).

tikatuwq 0.6.2

CRAN release: 2025-10-07

  • Fix: resolved codoc WARNING for generate_analysis() (docs matched to code).
  • No functional code changes.

tikatuwq 0.6.1

  • Maintenance update requested by CRAN.
  • Fixed relative link README-pt.md, now using absolute HTTPS URL.
  • No functional changes in code.

tikatuwq 0.6.0

  • New function plot_trend():
    • Visualize time series for parameters (e.g., turbidity, OD, IQA).
    • Add trend lines by group/point using three methods:
      • Theil–Sen (robust to outliers),
      • OLS (ordinary least squares),
      • LOESS (smoothed curve).
    • Supports faceting by river/point and customizable number of samples.
    • Returns a ggplot object ready for plotting.
  • Updated documentation for plot_trend() with practical examples.
  • Updated pkgdown site with dedicated section for trend visualization.
